Case Study Effects Co. browse by type volume/amplification amplification preamp / clean boost browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by enclosure pedal Case Study Aspen One - Boost + Overdrive Published on May 16, 2026 Case Study Effects Co. boost / preamp overdrive pedal Germanium Germanium Silicon Silicon Information The Case Study Aspen One combines the Aspen overdrive and a transparent MOSFET boost in a single true bypass enclosure with relay switching and an all-analog signal path. The Aspen overdrive section reworks an expandora-style circuit with increased post-drive output level and an added bass control for adjusting low-frequency response. Its gain range extends from edge-of-breakup overdrive to high-gain fuzz tones. The integrated MOSFET boost remains predominantly clean across most of its range and begins clipping when set to higher output levels. An internal order toggle changes the signal routing between boost into drive or drive into boost, producing substantially different gain structures and response characteristics. The pedal includes relay-based switching throughout and supports remote operation through a dedicated TRS control jack compatible with TRS-capable relay pedalboard switchers and external remote switches. Remote control functions allow activation of the Aspen side's SW1 function for increased gain or direct activation of the boost section from preset-based switching systems. The Aspen One also incorporates a revised fuzz mode derived from the original Aspen circuit. The updated implementation retains the aggressive character of the earlier design while improving stability and overall usability. Two clipping configurations are available. The Silicon version retains the clipping response of the original Aspen. The Germanium version uses hand-sourced vintage germanium diodes with softer clipping characteristics and smoother high-frequency response. While the pedal uses SMD board construction, the germanium diodes are hand-soldered individually. Production of the Germanium version depends on the remaining supply of the vintage diodes used in the circuit.
